task_instance: Using the ai-testing guidelines, write a robust, maintainable unit-test suite for a small sample UserService module (create_user success/duplicate-email paths, rename_user success/not-found paths), preferring a fake repository over mocks and including a contract test for the fake.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md (a test-design guidelines document). Created sample code under test at user_service.py (UserService with an injected UserRepository, DuplicateEmailError/UserNotFoundError, User dataclass). Created test_user_service.py applying the skill's guidance: a FakeUserRepository preferred over mocks; one behavior per test with descriptive names; distinct Arrange/Act/Assert phases; no logic in test bodies; state verification (asserting fake_repo.get(...) contents) rather than interaction verification; error-path tests asserting exception type via pytest.raises rather than exact messages; pytest fixtures for safe defaults; and a UserRepositoryContract base class run against the fake (section 8). The core deliverable (the test code) exists as text and its correctness was verified by manual trace of all 8 test cases against user_service.py: empty-repo create returns id '1' and persists; duplicate email raises before save so user '2' is never created; rename preserves id/email and updates name; unknown id raises; contract tests hold via dataclass equality. The runtime cannot execute pytest, so execution-based re-run (skill section 7) was not performed; verification was by static inspection/trace, which the skill itself sanctions ('tests should be trivially correct upon inspection'). Files: user_service.py, test_user_service.py, result.json in the work directory.
